speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Traffic Police will monitor and take action against drivers of vehicles with illegally modified exhaust systems that cause noise pollution along expressways, such as the East Coast Parkway; and (b) whether enhanced action can be taken against such drivers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Unfortunately, despite all the punitive actions to be taken, the problem does not seem to be mitigated.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, my Mountbatten residents are also complaining that vehicles travelling down the East Coast Parkway, because of their modified exhausts, are making a lot of noise.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, either we step up the enforcement or if I can ask the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) whether they would implement any other kind of regulations to deter people from modifying, speeding and creating noise at unearthly hours.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will not only look at the area but we also relate them to the different devices as well as information that each agency would have.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we will continue to look into the specific area that the Member has shared and see how we can address the issue.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, what is key is that we continue to monitor the situation in such issues that have been raised in certain areas.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, coming from the TP side, we work very closely with the ground and, if need be, we will also work with the community in the area.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: What is key is that we need to work together with the community as well as the whole-of-Government agencies.
